label: flash-slipstream
note: Slipstream serving its streaming package (the `prepared/` directory; its served model id is `local/<directory name>`, hence `local/prepared`). Point SLIPSTREAM_FLASH_MODEL at the package itself, not at the GGUF shard directory, so the harness's readiness wait does not have to sit through the one-time 5-7 minute preparation - build it once with `./slipstream serve --model <gguf dir>` and stop that server. --host 127.0.0.1 keeps it off the LAN; no --api-key so the harness's plain OpenAI requests work. Slipstream's defaults are left alone (MTP drafting with its confidence stop, prompt lookup for tool calls, one model server at a time); add SPLASH_EXPERT_CACHE_GIB or SPLASH_MAX_CONCURRENCY under `env` to measure a configuration rather than a default. Reference prompt lengths 4133 / 16286 are the frozen corpus prompts through Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's tokenizer and chat template with thinking off (the same numbers Kapitsa's and llama.cpp's Flash-Next configs use); if the harness's +/-1% check fails, it prints the counts it measured - record those here for this tokenizer.

label: flash-slipstream-plain
note: The same server with drafting effectively disabled (one guess, and only when the head is certain), for the same-engine baseline column: how much of Slipstream's decode is the target model alone.

label: flash-slipstream-llamacpp
note: The baseline the README compares against, under the harness's rules instead of a bespoke script: the same GGUF shard set Slipstream streams (set FLASH_NEXT_GGUF), -np 1 so both engines hold one sequence, -b/-ub 2048 (llama.cpp's default ubatch reads every expert once per 2048 rows), -lm none so its weights count in phys_footprint like Slipstream's, --min-p 0 because llama.cpp's default of 0.05 is not what the other configs measure, and the same explicit sampler. Pass the model's own chat template with --chat-template-file if its GGUF carries none, or the +/-1% prompt-length check will catch the drift. This row is optional: drop it if the point is only to place Kapitsa next to Slipstream on this Mac.
